claims.statement: linear-bot (packages/linear-bot) is a stateless Hono Cloudflare Worker that installs as Linear's native Agent: @mentions or assignments on issues arrive as AgentSessionEvent webhooks, the worker creates Open-Inspect coding sessions via the control plane, posts progress as Linear AgentActivities, and delivers terminal results back to the issue through signed control-plane callbacks.

POST /webhook verifies the raw body's HMAC-SHA256 against LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET using the linear-signature header (failure closes 401), shape-checks the payload (400), dedupes on the Linear-Delivery header via a 1-hour KV event:<deliveryId> entry, and then returns 200 immediately with all handling running in waitUntil — only AgentSessionEvent is handled, other event types log webhook.skipped.

Webhook dedupe keys on the Linear-Delivery header (a per-delivery UUID v4), never the body's webhookId, which is the constant registered-webhook configuration ID across deliveries — distinct deliveries sharing a webhookId are each processed.

handleAgentSessionEvent dispatches: a stop signal (agentActivity.signal === 'stop' or action stopped/cancelled) routes to stop handling; action 'prompted' on an issue with an existing KV issue:<issueId> mapping routes to the follow-up path; everything else attempts a new session; events without an issue log agent_session.no_issue and return.

Stop/cancel handling POSTs to /internal/sessions/<id>/stop for the mapped session and deletes the issue:<issueId> mapping; if the stop request fails (non-OK response), the mapping is deliberately retained so a later stop can still find the session.

A 'prompted' webhook on an issue whose KV mapping exists is always sent as an additional prompt to the existing session — never a new session; the handler builds a message-scoped callback context, fetches up to 500 characters of the most recent token event as best-effort 'Previous agent response' context, and POSTs /internal/sessions/<id>/prompt attributed to the follow-up author.

Callback context is message-scoped, not inherited by the control plane: every queued message (initial or follow-up) carries its own callbackContext with agentSessionId, organizationId, appUserId, issue, model, and tool-progress fields; a producer that queues a follow-up must attach it again, otherwise the control plane has no safe callback destination and skips completion delivery (observable as prompt.enqueue with has_callback_context:false).

New-session handling: resolves a Linear client (cached client-credentials token must match the webhook's appUserId), emits Thought activities, fetches full issue details, resolves the target, checks the integration enabled-repos gate, resolves model settings, POSTs to https://internal/sessions with repoOwner/repoName or environmentId (mutually exclusive) and actor signed as linear:<actorUserId>, stores the 7-day-TTL KV mapping, then POSTs the prompt to /internal/sessions/<id>/prompt with source 'linear' and callbackContext; failures emit Error activities.

The issue-to-session mapping is persisted in KV at issue:<issueId> with a 7-day expiration (86400*7), storing sessionId, issueId, issueIdentifier, target fields, model, agentSessionId, and createdAt; mappings older than the TTL expire, after which a follow-up cannot reach the session and a new request may start a new session.

Session target resolution is a five-stage cascade: 1) project → target KV mapping (highest priority), 2) team → target KV mapping (first label-matched entry, else first label-less default), 3) explicit owner/repo boundary-guarded match in the trigger or clarification-reply comment, 4) Linear's issueRepositorySuggestions API at >= 0.70 confidence, 5) LLM classification (Anthropic default, OpenAI supported); low confidence or failures emit an elicitation asking for owner/repo and create no session.

A session target is either a repository (owner/name) or a saved environment (stable env_… id); project and team mappings may name either kind while the suggestion and classification stages remain repository-only; an environment target's integration settings and callback repo resolve from its primary (first member) repository, and a mapped environment that no longer exists is skipped so resolution falls through to the next stage.

matchExplicitRepo finds the single available repository an owner/repo comment names, case-insensitively and boundary-guarded so acme/api does not match inside acme/api-legacy, notacme/api, not.acme/api, or acme/api.docs while ordinary terminal punctuation is accepted; naming zero or several repositories returns null so ambiguity still reaches the classifier.

Before creating a session, the resolved target's Linear integration config is fetched from the control plane (/internal/integration-settings/linear/resolved/<owner>/<name>); if enabledRepos is non-null and excludes the settings repository, an Error activity states the integration is not enabled and no session starts.

Model selection priority, highest first: a model:<name> issue label when allowLabelModelOverride is on (fixed map like haiku → anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5, opus-5, sonnet-5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.3-codex), the user's KV preference when allowUserPreferenceOverride is on, the repository override/global Linear default, then the deployment DEFAULT_MODEL; the winning model is normalized via getValidModelOrDefault and reasoning effort defaults per model.

Linear user preferences (user_prefs:<userId> storing { userId, model, reasoningEffort?, updatedAt }) are admin/API-managed KV entries, not set from a self-service Linear screen, and only apply when allowUserPreferenceOverride is on.

When no Linear integration settings are configured (or SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET is absent), the worker defaults to all accessible repositories in scope, user preferences and model:* labels allowed, and tool progress activities enabled.

POST /callbacks/tool_call emits ephemeral Action activities: edit_file/write_file → 'Edit' + filepath, read_file → 'Read' + filepath, bash/execute_command → 'Run' + command truncated to 80 chars with a non-empty parameter fallback, unknown tools use the tool name; it is skipped when agent context is missing or emitToolProgressActivities === false (older sessions default to enabled).

POST /callbacks/complete extracts the rich agent response from session events, emits the terminal Response activity (PR link, up to 10 file changes, 500-char summary) or Error activity, sets the agent session plan to completed/failed, and adds the Pull Request external URL when a PR artifact exists; Linear leaves 'Working' only after this terminal activity is delivered.

Completion delivery falls back to posting an issue comment via the legacy LINEAR_API_KEY only when the callback context lacks agentSessionId/organizationId/appUserId (or the client cannot be resolved); without LINEAR_API_KEY delivery is skipped and logged callback.no_linear_api_key, and a skipped completion cannot repair itself later.

Every /callbacks/* route requires a signed payload verified by rejectInvalidCallback: SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET must be configured (else 500), the in-body HMAC signature is verified over the original JSON key order using verifyCallbackFromControlPlane (failure 401), and each route then schema-parses before the guard.

POST /callbacks/start is invoked when the initial prompt is dispatched to a live sandbox: it verifies the signature, rejects stale callbacks (older than 5 minutes or more than 1 minute in the future), and only when context.transitionIssueOnStart === true moves the issue to the team's started state with a 20-second Linear budget; a skipped/rejected/timed-out/failed transition never blocks agent execution.

transitionIssueOnStart is set true only for action 'created' with a non-empty creatorId (human-initiated); automation-created sessions, already-mapped prompted events, and follow-ups get false or omit it, and follow-up prompts never change issue status.

transitionIssueToStarted queries the issue's workflow state type and the team's started states, no-ops for already_started/terminal_completed/terminal_canceled/no_started_state/issue_not_found, otherwise sorts started states by position and issues a single issueUpdate mutation to the lowest-position started state.

All issue-derived text (titles, descriptions, comments, promptContext, follow-ups, prior agent output) reaching the agent prompt is wrapped in <user_content source="…" author="…"> blocks with instruction-following disclaimers, and escaping closes the <user_content>/</user_content> tag shapes (including already-escaped variants) so untrusted text cannot break out or inject instructions.

Operator-managed config entries (config:team-repos, config:project-repos, user_prefs:<userId>) are validated key by key on read: a malformed entry is dropped and logged without invalidating sibling mappings, so a dropped valid mapping never silently falls through to classification heuristics; config keys are edited directly with wrangler kv key put, not via HTTP endpoints.

Team-to-target mapping entries may carry an optional label filter and an environment target may reference the stable env_… id; an entry carrying both an environmentId and repo keys resolves to its environment (environment-first ordering), and the first team entry without a label is the default fallback, while project mappings hold a single target and take the highest resolution priority.

Installation is OAuth2 with actor=app via GET /oauth/authorize and /oauth/callback: the authorization code is exchanged, the viewer identity (app user, organization) is fetched, the runtime client-credentials token is verified against that identity, and cached in KV; requires Linear workspace admin and app scopes read,write,app:assignable,app:mentionable.

Runtime API calls use OAuth2 client-credentials app-actor tokens (30-day) minted from the Linear client ID/secret, always verified against the fetched viewer identity: a token whose organization or appUserId mismatches the webhook is rejected; cached tokens live at oauth:client-credentials:<orgId>; authorization-code access/refresh tokens are not kept as runtime credentials and the legacy oauth:token:<orgId> record is deleted after the first successful client-credentials mint.

A cached client-credentials token is replaced on cache miss, near-expiry (5-minute skew), or an explicit HTTP 401 on a GraphQL request, which renews once and replays the identical rejected request; a second 401 throws client_credentials_rejected without another renewal, and concurrent issuance for the same (org, app-user) identity is shared in-flight while failed renewals are released for retry.

All Linear API interaction is raw GraphQL over fetch (no SDK — Workers cannot import CJS libraries) against https://api.linear.app/graphql with a 15-second timeout; AgentActivities are created via the agentActivityCreate mutation and agent session updates (plan, externalUrls) via agentSessionUpdate.

Repositories and environments are read from the control plane through a fail-open cached resource (in-memory 1-minute TTL → control plane → KV last-known-good copy with 5-minute TTL → empty fallback), so a control-plane read problem never blocks issue handling; malformed fresh bodies fall back to the KV copy instead of publishing 'no repositories'.

Repository classification calls the raw Anthropic or OpenAI API depending on CLASSIFICATION_MODEL (Anthropic default via ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OpenAI via OPENAI_API_KEY with strict structured output) with a forced tool call and shared timeout; no-repo, low-confidence, ambiguous, or provider-failure results degrade to an elicitation activity listing alternatives — never a guessed session.

Linear provides no Git credentials: repository access comes from the deployment's configured source-control integration (e.g., the GitHub App installation), and the Linear settings repository scope (enabledRepos allowlist) controls which resolved repositories can receive Linear-started sessions.
